title: Convergent Hosted Endpoint Lanes PRD and Launch Readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a single, predictable hosted API surface that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank use cases via explicit "lanes" and compatibility guarantees. Deliver a PRD that defines behavioral contracts, SLOs, SDK/CLI examples, migration paths, and a launch checklist with operational runbooks. This effort targets customers migrating from ad-hoc endpoint variants to a unified, production-ready hosted surface with developer ergonomics and cost/latency controls.
background: Multiple hosted endpoint variants have diverged across teams (legacy chat-v1, completions-lite, embeddings-v2, rerank-alpha). Customers want consistent semantics, documented fallbacks, and an easier migration path. This PRD formalizes lanes (interactive/chat, streamable-completions, embedding-vector, reranker) and defines acceptance gates for production launch.
scope: In-scope: API contract for 4 lanes (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank); streaming and non-streaming behavior; function/tool-calling primitives for chat; structured output support and JSON schema hints; embeddings dimensionality and normalization rules; rerank scoring API and batch sidecar; SDK examples (Python/Node); console dashboards for per-lane latency/cost. Out-of-scope: Multi-modal file upload support, model training pipelines, dedicated/private deployment packaging for this iteration.
requirements: Unified HTTP/REST and SDK surface: single /v1/hosted-endpoint with lane parameter and lane-specific payload schemas
Chat lane: support streaming tokens, tool/function calls, message history KV policy, P95 end-to-end latency targets (see SLOs)
Completions lane: non-streaming and streaming modes, temperature/top_p controls, max tokens, stop token handling, deterministic-seed test mode
Embeddings lane: predictable vector dims per model, L2-normalized output option, batching endpoint for up to 256 items per request
Rerank lane: accept candidate list + query, return score per candidate and optional top-N selector; support batch scoring and explainability hints
Error model: consistent error codes and retry semantics documented for transient vs client errors
Backwards compatibility: provide compatibility wrappers for existing hosted endpoints and clear migration guide
Operational: per-key rate limits, quotas, and soft-degrade fallback to cheaper model variants by policy
Observability hooks: tracing context propagation, token-level cost attribution, per-lane dashboards and alerting
non_goals: On-prem packaging and VPC private control plane (handled by Private team)
Building a separate legacy compatibility runtime — only wrapper adapters for migration
Full multi-modal (image/audio) support in this milestone
acceptance_criteria: API contract published with examples for all lanes and SDK code snippets
E2E integration tests passing in staging for each lane (baseline PRs + automated harness)

Latency SLOs validated under representative load: chat P95 <= 350ms for short-history requests; completions P95 <= 220ms for <=128 tokens; embeddings batch P95 <= 120ms per item at 64 batch; rerank P95 <= 180ms for 50 candidates
Cost-per-token/unit estimates documented and validated against Optimize recommendations
Console: per-lane dashboards wired to telemetry and a pre-launch alert set (error rate > 1% or latency SLO breach)
Canary rollout plan with progressive percentages and automatic rollback on SLO breach exists
Migration guide published and high-level customer communications drafted
Security review completed and KMS integration verified for hosted request logs retention policy
Billing flags and quotas enabled for all customers in staging and prod feature gates
success_metrics: >90% of public API calls use the unified endpoint within 90 days of GA for new signups
<0.5% incidence of breaking-contract bugs discovered post-launch during first 30 days
Observed token-cost reduction of >=10% for batched embedding workloads when using recommended settings
Meeting latency SLOs for >=95% of requests across lanes in production after rollout
launch_checklist: Finalize PRD and obtain PM/ENG/Design sign-off
Publish API spec (OpenAPI) and SDK changes (Python/Node) with example apps
Add compatibility wrappers and migration guide for legacy endpoints
Complete E2E and load testing in staging with runbook rehearsals
Create canary configuration (regions, % rollouts, rollback thresholds)
Enable per-lane telemetry dashboards and set alerting thresholds
Run security review checklist and confirm KMS/access controls
Document runbooks for common incidents (latency regressions, model fallback, quota exhaustion)
Train support and sales on behavioral changes, migration steps, and new pricing items
Tag release in repo and ensure release notes & changelog published
Open Post-launch monitoring epic and assign ownership for 30-day burn-in
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (internal): Roll out unified endpoint to internal teams and run compatibility tests for 2 weeks
Stage 2 (beta): Expose to 10% of developer signups and a small group of enterprise customers with target telemetry monitoring
Stage 3 (canary): Gradually increase to 50% across regions while watching SLOs and error rate
Stage 4 (GA): Full rollout with migration announcements and deprecation schedule for legacy endpoints
test_plan: Unit tests for lane-specific schema validation and parameter boundaries
Integration tests that verify streaming vs non-streaming behavior and function-calling semantics
Load tests that simulate combined traffic (chat-heavy, embedding-batch-heavy, rerank spikes) and validate autoscaling
Chaos scenario: GPU OOM/eviction simulation to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies
Regression suite: run historical prompt+output snapshot tests to detect quality regressions
dependencies: ENG-68212: Serving runtime batching improvements for stable latency
ENG-69821: Tracing and token-level cost telemetry plumbing
DES-21003: SDK examples and API documentation design
SEC-1044: KMS integration and logging retention policy
risks: Model compatibility: subtle behavioral differences between model variants could break downstream parsers
Latency regressions under mixed workloads if batching heuristics mis-tune
Customer confusion during migration if compatibility wrappers are incomplete
Billing gaps if per-lane cost attribution is miswired
mitigations: Ship adapter layer that normalizes responses for common client schemas
Run representative mixed-workload load tests and tune batching profiles in Optimize
Proactive customer communications with a migration timeline and sample code
Smoke billing tests in staging and gated billing enablement during canary
notes: Design asked for a single payload entrypoint to reduce onboarding friction — engineering proposed lane parameter to keep routing logic explicit.
PM to coordinate pricing and billing adjustments with finance before GA.
Recommend feature flag per-customer to enable experimental rerank explainability metadata.
